en.html:
By now, even the words for how I felt had run out.

Fire.
All around us, fire roaring away.

A wildfire? No ceiling. Earth and grit underfoot. At least we did not seem to be indoors. Grass, leaves, trees—that was what was burning.

—No. Not only that.

en.html:
The burning hell of the Commedia, the Divine Comedy.

It took no wit to think of that name here. Even I, a man with no particular talent in that direction, could manage it. All I had to do was look honestly at what was in front of me.

People were burning.
People. People. Too many to count.

I could not tell their race or sex. Already burned black, but still unmistakably human in shape. The shape of something that had been alive. What was left of it.

I stood there alone among the flames and bodies. My armour let me endure the heat with a toughness I felt ashamed to possess.

...What had happened here?

Just a fire? Unfortunate victims?

If I chose to look at it that way, perhaps. But once I began asking questions, there was no end to them.

Why had they died here, gathered together like this? Why had they not scattered and escaped?

Or had escape been impossible?
—Why?

ja.html:
かの〝<ruby>神曲<rt>コンメディア</rt></ruby>〟に謳われる火炎地獄。
　
　ここでその名を出す事は、およそ洒落心などに無縁
の人間であっても――つまり俺でも、容易であった。

　ただ素直に視覚情報を評価すれば、そう思える。

　焼けているのは人だった。
　数え切れない人、人、人。

　人種も性別もわからない。皆とうに焼け焦げて炭化
している。しかし原形は留めていて、間違いなく人間
だとわかる。
　生命あるものの形だった。その残骸だった。

　火炎と死屍の中、ぽつんと佇む。
　甲鉄に覆われた俺は、後ろめたさを覚える頑強さで
火の猛威に耐えていられた。

　……この光景は何なのだろう。

　単なる火災と、不幸な犠牲者なのか？
　そう見ればそう見える。だが疑念を抱けば、それは
際限なく広がってゆく。

　どうしてこんな所で、このように集まって焼死して
いるのか。
　逃げ散れば良いだろうに。

　それとも、逃げられなかったのだろうか。
　――何故？

A little different?
Different from the Emishi...?

The Western Emishi—the Judea, the white Emishi?

With that thought, I looked at the ground. The plants did not look like Yamato's. More like Europe's.

White Emishi. Europe. All these deaths.
...Something was almost joining up in my mind...

I stopped and looked toward where the figure had been. The flames shifted widely again and showed her to me.

A small body. Exceptionally pale skin. Long ears—
It seemed I had guessed correctly. At least this one survivor had the features of the white Emishi.

She did not seem to have noticed us. Dazed, staring at the flames that were about to close around her.

—She.

　読みは当たっていたらしい。少なくともその唯一の
生存者は白蝦夷の特徴を備えていた。

　<ruby>彼女<rt>・・</rt></ruby>はこちらに気付いていないようだ。
　自失の態で、己を包み込もうとする炎の渦に視線を
注いでいる。

　――彼女。

The moment I realised she was female, something flashed through my mind. I knew her. I had met her once.

At the Yokohama base.
Professor Wolf and Chachamaru had introduced her to me—the Forged Bomb.

That girl who had seemed hollow inside.

en.html:
Why was she here?

...No. That was not the question to be asking myself now. That mystery could wait.

Was I going to leave her? Truly leave her to die?

What did I know about her, in the end? Nothing. I was not even certain she had really been part of the Forged Bomb.

Not one proper reason for thinking it was all right to abandon her.

Only what I could see was certain. A white Emishi girl, caught in the flames, about to die.

Was I not going to save her?

If I did, I would not return to our own time and place. No one in that world would be left to stop the 'god'. How much would be lost then?

ja.html:
何故ここに？

　……いや、違う。
　いま自身の心に問うべきは、そんな緊急性のない謎
ではない。

　助けなくて良いのか。
　本当に見捨てて良いのか。

　結局のところ、俺は彼女について何も知らない。
　本当に鍛造雷弾の一部であったのか、それすら確信
はない。

　見捨てて良いと思える根拠は全くない。

　確かな事は、いま目に見えている事実のみだ。
　白蝦夷の少女が、炎に巻かれて死のうとしている。

　助けなくて良いのか。

　助ければ、俺は元の時空間へ戻れなくなる。
　あの世界で〝神〟を止められる者はいなくなり――
結果、どれほどのものが失われるだろうか。
